description: The frontend's Memory surface: what it may render about deliberately retained knowledge, and what it must never become. Memory is ONE LEGO (`memory`, index 4 of the official AI/Agent set, phase B) with ONE contract (`ai.memory`) — it is not a sub-LEGO of `context-session` and it is not a sixteenth top-level LEGO. The catalog ships EMPTY on purpose: this is a record surface, so it renders what it is handed and names every absence. `Context` is what is loaded now and can be replaced; `Memory` is what was retained and must survive that replacement.

publication.note: `publication.rows` carries only what THIS tree publishes, and protected main @ 67e638ef publishes no `ai.memory` row — so against it the surface reports declared-not-locked and renders no version. Agent-2 published the row on its own branch (see publishedOnPeerBranch); the surface derives `published` from the rows it is handed, so the same code reports `published at 1.0.0` against that tree with no edit.

rules: Memory survives context replacement. Context is what is loaded now and can be compacted, rolled over and replaced; Memory is what was deliberately retained and must still be there afterwards. A record REFERENCES a context, session or run through `references` and never contains one.

Every shared word is quoted from the published contract with provenance: 5 scopes, 6 kinds, 5 retentions, 13 fields, 2 lifecycle states, 10 graph nodes, 11 graph edges, 4 published operations (`memory.remember`, `memory.recall`, `memory.list`, `memory.forget`) and 2 permission words (`ai:memory:read`, `ai:memory:write`). Nothing is coined here.

The words the contract does NOT publish have no set at all: there is no embedding, no similarity, no relevance score and no retention timer, so a screen cannot render them even by accident. `traverse` and `relate` are declared future stages and are named as deferred rather than offered.
Operations are spelled exactly as published (`memory.remember`, not `ai.memory.remember`): a consumer that re-qualifies a published name has invented a second API.

The published operation names are facts, not affordances. Nothing here calls one, and no rendered list offers remember, forget or restore — `memory.forget` is terminal, has no undo and no restore operation exists to offer.

Scope owns isolation: `GLOBAL` has no owner and every other scope requires a `scopeOwner` that is a stable identity. A request for an unknown scope, or a non-GLOBAL scope without an owner, is refused rather than widened to the nearest namespace.

Retrieval is deterministic and bounded: `memory.list` filters by scope, scopeOwner, kind and retention, orders `createdAt` ascending then `memoryId` ascending, clamps `limit` to 1..100 (default 50) and pages by opaque cursor. The surface re-sorts nothing, because no ranking is published to sort by.

Four list states, never three: `rendered`, `empty` (the backend answered zero matches — an answer, not an error), `not-handed-over` (nobody asked, so nothing is claimed) and `refused` (the payload broke the quoted vocabulary and the refusal is named). Collapsing `empty` into `not-handed-over` is how a UI tells a user their memory was erased.

Persistence is behind a provider boundary, so it is never claimed: exactly three statements — `provider-bound`, `in-memory-only`, `not-declared`. No 'saved', no 'synced', no connected indicator for a provider the surface cannot see, and no durability implied by a record being on screen.

Integrity is reported, never repaired: a record carries the two-field envelope (size, checksum) and a checksum that is not a 64-character lowercase sha256 hex digest is reported as a finding. The surface verifies nothing itself — it refuses to render a digest in a shape the contract does not publish.

No credentials, tokens, secrets, cookies, authorization headers, chain-of-thought, raw or hidden prompts, transcripts, message lists, full model output, host paths or capability grants — refused by name and by key pattern (`security.sensitiveRefusal` in the contract is the same rule).
Records are supplied to the runtime by the application; this package never reads the backend tree, never writes a record, and nothing it returns enters the 18,126-byte boot descriptor.

A declaration whose vocabulary moved past the quote is reported (`memoryDrift`) with both spellings and is never adopted silently; a version claimed in a file is reported as `declaredVersion` and is still not a publication.

alignment.rule: A difference between this package's quoted vocabulary and the declaration it consumes is reported as data (memoryDrift) and registered, never resolved by adopting a word this package cannot quote. There is no tolerated difference: REGISTERED_DRIFT in test/29 is empty.
alignment.openHalf: XA-12 is open for exactly the half the contract defers: relevance-ranked traversal, explicit edge creation and retention-policy enforcement. None of the three changes what this surface may render today, and none of them may be implied by it.
relatedDecisions: XA-11 (where Skill and Memory are modelled — this surface adds no domain and no LEGO: `ai.memory` stays a capability of `ai-foundation` and `memory` stays index 4 of the AI set)
XA-20 (Context & Session publication — unchanged by P2.14; the two surfaces consume two different contracts and neither absorbs the other)
XA-21 (descriptor-assembly heap pin, 4,096 KB — NOT touched by P2.14: the Memory view is built on demand and the pin is not edited)
